original_question: Construct a natural Hamiltonian system with a nonconstant potential on S 2 that admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of degree 5 and does not admit any nontrivial integrals of smaller degrees.
target_in_paper: Problem 2.5 in §2.1.1 of the arXiv v1 PDF (the same item appears as Problem 3.5 in §3.1.1 of the current arXiv HTML rendering): the sphere case isolated after the table row where degree at least 5 is described as largely open. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target almost verbatim: it has the correct manifold S^2, the correct class of systems (natural Hamiltonian systems with nonconstant potential), the correct integrability class (polynomial in momenta), the correct target degree (5), and the correct exclusion of all smaller nontrivial degrees. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
missing_details: The phase space is the cotangent bundle T^*S^2 with its canonical symplectic structure; the problem is not posed directly on S^2 itself. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

A natural Hamiltonian system here means a Hamiltonian of the form H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j+U(x), where g is a metric on S^2 and U:S^2→R is a nonconstant function. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

An integral should be made explicit as a first integral F satisfying {H,F}=0, and the relevant class is that F is polynomial in the momenta p with coefficients depending on x. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

The degree is the total degree in the momenta, and the phrase 'smaller degrees' should be unpacked as degrees 1, 2, 3, and 4 within the class of polynomial-in-momenta first integrals. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

The paper declares H itself and all functions of H to be trivial integrals, so 'nontrivial' should be stated as 'not a function of H'. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it is best to specify the smooth real setting: smooth metric, smooth potential, and smooth real-valued coefficient functions in the polynomial integral. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

No extra hypotheses from nearby problems belong here: not flatness, not analyticity, not magnetic terms, and not superintegrability. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
refined_question: Construct a smooth natural Hamiltonian system on T^*S^2 with canonical symplectic structure, namely a Hamiltonian H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j+U(x) for some smooth metric g on S^2 and nonconstant smooth potential U:S^2→R, such that there exists a nontrivial first integral F with {H,F}=0 where F is a real polynomial of total degree 5 in the momenta p with smooth x-dependent coefficients, and such that H admits no nontrivial polynomial-in-momenta first integrals of degrees 1, 2, 3, or 4. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
equivalent_formulation: Construct a natural Hamiltonian system with nonconstant potential on S^2 whose smallest degree of a nontrivial polynomial integral in momenta is 5. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because the paper first defines natural Hamiltonian systems and polynomial integrals, then explains in the two-dimensional case that the sphere remains largely open starting at degree at least 5, and finally isolates exactly the degree-5 sphere problem as Problem 2.5/3.5. The Kiyohara discussion immediately above it explains why 'degree 5 and no smaller degrees' is the sharp formulation: existing S^2 geodesic examples of degree d at least 3 are only known to exclude degrees 1 and 2, not intermediate degrees. The draft should therefore not be broadened to the torus conjectures, to magnetic Hamiltonians, or to the superintegrability problem, which are neighboring but distinct items. No homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large m' clause is part of this target statement. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
